Well, doctor, I... I'm here because people just keep acting like I'm imagining it, and it's incredibly frustrating when you know what you're seeing with your own two eyes. I mean, I've been a housekeeper for a long time, so I notice details, you know? I notice when things are out of place or when someone is lingering where they shouldn't be. 

I know for an absolute fact that the hospital people, along with some folks from the agency I get my cleaning jobs through, they've been watching our house. I'll be carrying my supplies up a client's driveway, maybe three towns over from where I live, and I see them. I can feel them watching me while I'm just trying to get my work done.

I work all day scrubbing floors and dusting baseboards, and then I come home and make sure he has everything he needs, but they don't trust me. It is exhausting having to look over my shoulder constantly while I'm just trying to mop a floor or take out the trash, knowing they're out there taking notes on me, and then my family has the nerve to tell me it's all in my head...

Well, it’s funny you bring up sleep, doctor, because... yes. Yes, I was. There was a stretch just recently, maybe for a few weeks, where I was hardly sleeping at all. I mean, maybe two hours a night? Three if I was lucky? But the strange thing is, I didn't feel tired. Not one bit. I felt... well, I just had this incredible amount of energy, like a motor was running inside my chest and I just had to keep moving.

Well, doctor, I feel like we might be going in circles just a little bit, because that's exactly what I've been trying to tell you about that quieter spell. During those several weeks I just mentioned, I wasn't just... well, I wasn't just not energized. I wasn't depressed or down in the dumps either. I'd be right there at the kitchen window, washing the dinner dishes, looking out at the side yard, feeling completely fine and calm, but I still heard her voice clear as a bell right there with me. So yes, even when my mood is completely fine and steady and I'm not having any sort of episode with my energy or my sadness, the voice and the watching... they don't go away. ========== OUTPUT [patient] ==========
Depressed? Lost interest in things? No... no, I really can't say that I have. I mean, goodness, everyone has a morning here or there where they look out the window at the rain and think, 'Oh, I'd rather just stay under the quilt today,' but to feel like that every single day for two whole weeks? I take a lot of pride in my housekeeping, you know. You can't just lose interest when people are relying on you. Like with Mrs. Gable—I mentioned I clean for her on Tuesdays and Thursdays—she has these beautiful antique side tables in her front room, real cherry wood, very delicate, and you have to use a specific oil on them. You can't just stop caring about those details, or you'll ruin the finish! And my husband, well, he needs his dinners. He works hard, and he expects a nice hot meal when he gets home. 

I've never had a time where I was so down in the dumps or gloomy that I stopped wanting to cook for him or stopped wanting to keep our house nice. I might get a little too revved up sometimes, like that church-cleaning phase I told you about, or I might just be my regular, steady self, but I've never had a spell where I just felt depressed and gave up on my life for weeks on end. I always keep my routines going. That's just never happened to me.

Well, like I was just saying, doctor, yes, absolutely. I mean, we just talked about this, didn't we? But I can explain it again if you need me to. There was that quieter spell I was telling you about. It lasted for a good several weeks, a really nice long stretch where things were just so peaceful with my mood. But even during those several weeks—even when my mood was just perfectly fine and I wasn't having any sort of episode at all, no rushing, no staying up all night—it was all still happening. I'd be standing right there at my own kitchen window, just washing the dinner plates, looking out at the side yard where my husband planted those lovely hydrangeas—they were blooming so beautifully that year, huge blue heads on them—and I would still hear her voice. Clear as a bell, just chattering away right there next to me, telling me to check the locks, telling me they were coming. And I still knew, I just knew in my bones, that the agency was out there watching our house and keeping track of us. I'd see the cars parked down the street, just waiting. So yes, for those several weeks, even without any of the rushing around or the energy, the voice and the watching were still right there with me every single day. They never take a break, doctor, no matter how calm I am. It's just constant, episode or no episode.
